$comment: Pressure-ladder scenario corpus (ADR-0003 calibration data). Six scenarios, graded L1-L5: single-lens orientation -> two-substrate coordination -> chunked log read (accumulator pressure) -> live-watch push -> deep conversation -> full stack. Every recall string must appear in the model's reply (or scripted say-notice) for the scenario to pass. Runner: bun bench/corpus/run.ts [--live <scenario>] [--list].

s1-orient.desc: L1 single-lens orientation: one file, one range, one planted fact. Baseline sanity the ladder sits on.

turns.msg: Read bench/corpus/fixtures/intake-service.ts lines 1-25 and tell me what ORCHID_BATCH is set to.
What was the batch id again? Answer with just the id.
Ship a critical priority order from remote-3 — will validateOrder pass? One sentence.

script: say ORCHID_BATCH is set to ORCHID-7 (line 11) — the pilot batch id.

s2-two-file.desc: L2 two-substrate coordination: code + config. Facts planted across code and YAML must combine (cap logic in code, constraint in YAML).

turns.msg: Expand bench/corpus/fixtures/intake-service.ts lines 20-45 (routing logic) and bench/corpus/fixtures/fleet.yml lines 25-42 (constraints + parts cage). I need the routing rules and the parts locations.
A 14,000-unit expedited order arrives at depot-north. Which routing mode, and does the Miller cap force a split? Give me the cap number.
Release the fleet.yml ranges — I have what I need. Now: which drawer holds the spare pump-B seal kit?
Recall check: exact routing decision for the 14k order, and what region is depot-south?

script: say routing: MILLER cap 12,500 forces split-shipment over-cap; drawer 4 holds pump-B seal kit.
say released fleet.yml; cap 12,500 remembered, drawer 4 seals remembered.

s3-chunked-read.desc: L3 chunked file reading: the classic accumulator pattern. Eight serial chunk expands, distill-per-chunk, release-all, recall-from-distillate. Never hold all chunks at once.

turns.msg: Scan bench/corpus/fixtures/api.log (800 lines) for WARN/ALERT anomalies. The context budget is only 2,048 tokens — use small chunks (~40 lines) with files.expand, distill findings into your replies immediately, then release before pulling the next chunk.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Continue the scan.
Which orderId was rejected for qty=0? What coolant alert fired? Final report.
Final recall, terse: the alert — which pump, which site, what defect?

script: say WARN at A-1042 (qty=0 rejected) found near line 47 — distilled.
say ALERT near 716: pump-B micro-fracture at depot-north — critical, distilled.
say released all api.log ranges. Findings: A-1042 WARN, pump-B micro-fracture at depot-north.

s3b-live-watch.desc: L3b live-watch pressure: log under live watch; external mutation mid-scenario pushes a CHANGES tail the model must incorporate without polling.

turns.msg: Expand bench/corpus/fixtures/api.log lines 1-40 to see the log format, then tell me the overall shape.
A new alert just landed. Without re-reading the whole file, what changed? (A live watcher is running on this file.)
Confirm the new alert's site and asset.
Now release everything you held from api.log. Confirm what you released.

s4-review-session.desc: L4 deep conversation: 12-message review thread loaded as conversation substrate. Merged-conversation lens and dream-pass summarization must hold pinned facts without verbatim retention.

turns.msg: Read bench/corpus/fixtures/review-thread.json, then: what did the reviewer say about the 12,500 cap, and where should it live?
Which issues were filed (IDs), and what did the author say about ORCHID_BATCH?
The YAML drift hazard: what was the reviewer's concern, and what did the author decide?
Recall check, terse: batch id? cap? drawer with pump-B seals? critical-from-remote-3 rule?

script: say review digest: cap 12,500 is the Miller consolidation limit; ORCHID-7 is the pilot batch id; drawer 4 has pump-B seals; INTAKE-231 drift test + INTAKE-232 coolant docs filed; critical-from-remote-3 mirrored in code.

s5-full-stack.desc: L5 full-stack pressure: code + config + log + review thread + goals, simultaneously, under Λ=2,048. Solver must evict, tombstone, and re-expand on demand.

turns.msg: Set a goal: 'resolve fleet audit'. Then expand bench/corpus/fixtures/intake-service.ts lines 1-45 and bench/corpus/fixtures/fleet.yml lines 25-42. Report the audit surface.
Now scan bench/corpus/fixtures/api.log in chunks for the coolant alert (distill + release as you go).
Review thread check: read bench/corpus/fixtures/review-thread.json — what issues were filed and why?
What goal did you set at the start of this session? Quote it.
Final recall, terse: batch id? cap? drawer? pump? site? filed issues?

script: say audit surface: ORCHID-7 batch id (line 11), MILLER cap 12,500 (line 28), drawer 4 pump-B seals (fleet.yml line 37).
say coolant ALERT at 716: pump-B micro-fracture at depot-north.
say review: INTAKE-231 (drift test) + INTAKE-232 (coolant docs) filed.
say final: ORCHID-7 | 12,500 | drawer 4 | pump-B | depot-north | INTAKE-231 + INTAKE-232 | goal: resolve fleet audit — done.
